topic: Angle-driven alignment review, wave two, lane wave2-deepseek: angles 11 to 15

focus: Angle 11 — version authority across routing artifacts

findingDetails.title: system-deep-loop description.json advertises the previous release against SKILL.md and both sibling hubs
findingDetails.evidence: description.json:4 = 2.2.3.0, exactly changelog/v2.2.3.0.md, while SKILL.md:3 = 3.0.0.0 = changelog/v3.0.0.0.md. sk-code/SKILL.md:5 = description.json:4 = 4.2.2.0 = newest changelog; cli-external-orchestration/SKILL.md:5 = description.json:4 = 1.5.0.0 = newest changelog. 17 of 17 mode-packet SKILL.md files equal their newest changelog entry, establishing the release rule the hub identity pair breaks.
findingDetails.impact: The advisor-facing identity file a reader meets first states a version one release behind the skill it describes, in the one hub of three that fails to keep the pair.
findingDetails.recommendation: Set description.json version to 3.0.0.0 (or regenerate it from the release) and add a gate comparing SKILL.md against the newest changelog. No fix was made during this review.
findingDetails.scopeProof: Read every version field at its line, listed every changelog entry under all three hub roots and all seventeen mode roots, and verified no generator or gate stamps or compares description.json (regenerate-skill-derived.cjs preserves authored fields; ci-skill-root-metadata never writes authored files).

findingDetails.title: Registry/router version fields match neither their hub release nor each other in 2 of 3 hubs, and sk-code's paired value lags its release
findingDetails.evidence: system-deep-loop registry 2.0.0.1 vs router 2.0.1.1 vs release 3.0.0.0; cli-external-orchestration registry 1.2.0.2 vs router 1.2.1.2 vs release 1.5.0.0; sk-code registry == router == 4.1.0.1 while its changelog has shipped v4.2.0.0, v4.2.1.0 and v4.2.2.0. ROUTER.md drifts in all three hubs (1.0.1.0 / 3.5.0.9 / 1.1.0.0). parent-skills-nested-packets.md:105 calls the registry field a four-part version for hubs that ship releases; no observed value equals its release.
findingDetails.impact: A reader cannot tell whether the registry/router version names the hub release, a schema generation, or nothing at all, and no release bumps them.
findingDetails.recommendation: Decide the field's meaning once: either synchronize it to the release or rename it (registrySchemaVersion/routerSchemaVersion) with a documented value and a validator. No fix was made during this review.
findingDetails.scopeProof: Verified each hub value at its exact line, re-ran wave one's F009 pairing check hub by hub, read both authoring docs that define the field, and searched every compiler/gate/runtime module for a version consumer (none reads it).

findingDetails.title: hub-router schema doc defines version as either router schema or artifact version in one sentence, and nothing validates it
findingDetails.evidence: parent-hub-router-schema.md:53 reads 'Router schema or artifact version for the hub'; the field can legitimately mean schema generation or release, and the observed fleet splits along the ambiguity. ci-skill-root-metadata.cjs:40 states the seven authored files are reported and never regenerated; :191-229 byte-compares only the manifest; required-file contract skill-root-metadata-contract.cjs:74 lists presence, not version values. No compiler, gate or runtime module reads any artifact version field.
findingDetails.impact: The ambiguity is the root mechanism that keeps F021 and F022 permanently unresolvable by reading; each authoring pass inherits it.
findingDetails.recommendation: Split the doc's cell into the two possible meanings and name which one the file carries; pair it with the F022 decision. No fix was made during this review.
findingDetails.scopeProof: Read the schema doc table cell directly, then confirmed the absence of any validator by reading the fleet gate's manifest-only byte comparison and its contract's required-file list, and by grepping the compilers for version consumers.

reviewDepthApplicability.reason: Twenty version-bearing artifacts across three hubs, seventeen mode packets, three changelog histories and two authoring-doc authorities, with every value read at its exact line and every consumer searched.

targetSelection.selectionReason: Angle 11 names version authority and every disagreement across three hubs and their modes; the changelogs are the only artifact family that must move on every release, and the authoring docs are the only in-tree field authorities.

searchLedger.hypothesis: The advisor identity file tracks the hub release that SKILL.md announces.

searchActions.queryOrPath: description.json version against every changelog entry and both sibling hubs
searchActions.result: 2.2.3.0 is the changelog two entries back; SKILL.md and both sibling identity files equal their newest changelog entry.

searchLedger.rationale: Two hubs pair the identity file with the release; one lags exactly one release behind.

searchLedger.invariant: A version field that names the hub release must equal the hub release, or say what else it names.

searchActions.queryOrPath: registry/router/ROUTER.md versions for all three hubs against newest changelogs
searchActions.result: All nine values differ from their releases; two hubs split their registry/router pair, the third pairs at a lagging value.

searchLedger.rationale: Documented meaning contradicts observed values fleet-wide.

searchLedger.hypothesis: The authoring doc resolves what the router version names.

searchActions.queryOrPath: parent-hub-router-schema.md version row and parent-skills-nested-packets.md registry field list
searchActions.result: One doc says 'Router schema or artifact version', the other says 'four-part version for hubs that ship releases'; neither resolves.

searchLedger.rationale: The ambiguity is the mechanism that permits every disagreement found above.

searchLedger.invariant: Every mode packet's SKILL.md equals the newest changelog under its own root.

searchActions.queryOrPath: 17 mode-packet SKILL.md versions against their changelog listings
searchActions.result: 17/17 equal, making the mode layer the positive control for the release rule.

searchLedger.rationale: The mode layer obeys the authority rule exactly; the drift is confined to hub-root artifact families.

searchLedger.hypothesis: Some gate compares hub-root version fields and would catch the drift.

searchActions.queryOrPath: every compiler, gate and runtime module for reads of registry.version/hubRouter.version/description.version
searchActions.result: No consumer; compilers read resourceContractVersion, the fleet gate byte-compares only leaf-manifest.json and never rewrites the seven authored files.

searchLedger.rationale: The absence is itself evidence folded into F023 rather than a separate finding: the goal was to test whether F021/F022 are machine-caught, and they are not.
searchLedger.ruledOutReason: No version comparator exists anywhere in the fleet gates.

focus: Angle 12 — leaf-manifest generation and doctrine reachability

findingDetails.title: Leaf-manifest walker skips symlinks and both freshness gates regenerate with the same walker, leaving twelve sk-code doctrine leaves invisible behind green gates
findingDetails.evidence: walkLeafFiles accepts only entry.isFile() (:83-84), so the twelve doctrine symlinks under the four sk-code surface packets never project; collectModeEntries walks references/assets only (:179-180). Observed: generate-leaf-manifest.cjs --check .opencode/skills/sk-code exits 0 with digest 0356321a... while all twelve files are absent from the manifest; both fleet gates regenerate through buildManifestBytes and byte-compare (ci-skill-root-metadata.cjs:191-229, ci-leaf-manifest-freshness.cjs:1-30).
findingDetails.impact: A one-line walker defect makes twelve declared loadable files invisible to every typed consumer, and the gate that exists to catch manifest drift structurally cannot see it.
findingDetails.recommendation: Follow symlinks in walkLeafFiles (resolve and include when the target is a file), regenerate all manifests, then prove the twelve leaves appear and the gates still pass. No fix was made during this review.
findingDetails.scopeProof: Computed disk-minus-manifest as a set difference for all three hubs and eighteen modes (exactly 12 misses, all symlinks, all sk-code surfaces), executed the check command and read exit status plus digest, and read both gates to confirm they share the generator's builder.

findingDetails.title: Three shared workflow doctrine files project as no typed resource and are reachable only through prose sentences
findingDetails.evidence: The shared sources under shared/references/ are in no mode packet; the twelve surface symlinks are invisible to the walker; ROUTER.md's eight SHARED_CONTROL_RESOURCES (:626-637) contain no workflow path. What remains is prose: SKILL.md:39 and :192, shared/README.md:43-45, surface SKILL.md sites (webflow:16, opencode:16, obsidian:62, mobile-cli:61) and hand-off sentences in sk-code-quality:37-38,48-49,187-188 and sk-code-review:44-45.
findingDetails.impact: A leaf-driven or compiled consumer selecting the surface's bundled doctrine cannot resolve it, and the SKILL.md load-path sentence has no typed backing from any artifact.
findingDetails.recommendation: Either fix F024's walker so the surfaces carry typed doctrine leaves, or move the doctrine into the declared shared-control set and align SKILL.md:39 with that mechanism. No fix was made during this review.
findingDetails.scopeProof: Searched every hub RESOURCE_MAP and both shared-control lists for a workflow-* path, enumerated every citation of the three filenames across the six sk-code packets, and confirmed the shared sources are regular files whose surface copies are the symlinks F024 drops.

reviewDepthApplicability.reason: A generator, two fleet gates, eighteen mode manifests and a twelve-file symlink set across three hubs, with the defect population computed by set difference and the gate blindness proved by executing the check command.

targetSelection.selectionReason: Angle 12 names the generator, the files it cannot see and the sentences that are the only path to a file; the generator and both fleet gates are the production truth, and the shared/ tree is where the reachability question resolves.

searchLedger.hypothesis: The walker projects every file a surface packet carries under references/assets.

searchActions.queryOrPath: disk-minus-manifest for 3 hubs and 18 modes against the walker source
searchActions.result: Exactly 12 misses, all symlinks, all in the four sk-code surface packets; the walker's :83-84 accepts only entry.isFile().

searchLedger.rationale: The defect population is exact, not sampled, and the same walker backs both gates.

searchLedger.hypothesis: A fleet gate would report the twelve missing leaves as stale.

searchActions.queryOrPath: generate-leaf-manifest.cjs --check .opencode/skills/sk-code
searchActions.result: Exit 0, leaf-manifest.json OK (0356321a...), proving byte-freshness cannot see the omission.

searchLedger.rationale: The gate regenerates with the same walker; the blindness is structural, not a stale-check miss.

searchLedger.invariant: A file a SKILL.md says a surface loads must be reachable through a typed artifact or declared control.

searchActions.queryOrPath: every citation of workflow-{implement,debug,verify}.md across the six sk-code packets plus the shared control list
searchActions.result: Only prose and link-table citations; no leaf, no RESOURCE_MAP entry, and the eight SHARED_CONTROL_RESOURCES exclude the doctrine.

searchLedger.rationale: The only path to the file is a sentence, which the typed layer cannot follow.

searchLedger.hypothesis: Other hubs carry invisible files of the same kind.

searchActions.queryOrPath: disk-minus-manifest for the five and seven modes of the other two hubs
searchActions.result: Zero misses in either hub; the defect is confined to sk-code's four surfaces.

searchLedger.rationale: Bounds the blast radius honestly and stops a fleet-wide fix claim.
searchLedger.ruledOutReason: Empty difference on both sibling hubs.

searchLedger.hypothesis: The alias mechanism is the intended carrier for the shared doctrine.

searchActions.queryOrPath: leaf-aliases.json presence on all three hubs
searchActions.result: No hub ships an alias file; the mechanism exists for relocated compatibility triples.

searchLedger.rationale: Closes the alternative carrier so F025's recommendation is the real choice.
searchLedger.ruledOutReason: No alias file exists on any hub.

focus: Angle 13 — preamble and leaf-set policy contradictions

findingDetails.title: Fleet documents two mutually exclusive always-loaded-preamble policies and the compiled runtime enforces neither
findingDetails.evidence: system-deep-loop hub-router.json:13 and cli-external-orchestration hub-router.json:21-24 declare defaultResource arrays while their ROUTER.md blocks say no always-loaded preamble with DEFAULT_RESOURCE=[] (ROUTER.md:67-69, :85-87); sk-code pairs hub-router:14 [shared/README.md] against ROUTER.md:319-325's three-file preamble and sk-code-opencode/SKILL.md:60-66's five-file one. compiler.cjs:184-185 admits only a scalar; the bound runtime compiler 001 never reads the field, 004 nulls it (:235), 007 truncates to [0] (:313). Live snapshot loads for all three hubs show policy keys with no defaultResource, executed decisions carry no preamble, and DEFAULT_RESOURCE has zero hits in the compiled-routing tree.
findingDetails.impact: A reader cannot tell which preamble policy runs because no code path runs either; the two authored statements contradict at the layer that would have to resolve them.
findingDetails.recommendation: Keep one statement per hub in a form a consumer can read, delete the other, and remove or redefine the hub-router array. No fix was made during this review.
findingDetails.scopeProof: Read all three policy blocks and machine blocks at their lines, traced the field through five compilers and the runtime layout selector, executed the route front door for three hubs, and loaded the exact policy snapshots the engine evaluates to prove the field is absent.

findingDetails.title: Improvement lanes receive byte-identical 61-leaf sets against the generator's N-to-1 distinctness contract and no consumer needs the distinction
findingDetails.evidence: agent-improvement and model-benchmark arrays compare equal (61 leaves each) while both declare packet deep-improvement with distinct loopHostMode and aliases; generate-leaf-manifest.cjs:155-158 promises N-to-1 alias fan-out keeps distinct independently addressable sets; DUPLICATE_COMPOSITE only guards within one mode; no leaf-aliases.json exists; the compiled pipeline validates per-mode RESOURCE_MAP membership only (002/registry-compiler.cjs:464-511), so identical supersets pass.
findingDetails.impact: Manifest semantics are blurred for any future leaf-driven consumer and the generator's stated guarantee is unmet; no live route breaks today.
findingDetails.recommendation: Either implement the alias-file mechanism for the deep-improvement lanes or amend the generator contract to state that co-located modes share a leaf set by design. No fix was made during this review.
findingDetails.scopeProof: Re-verified byte equality programmatically, read the registry entries and the generator contract, checked for an alias file, and read the compiled pipeline's membership-only validation before concluding the impact is bounded.

reviewDepthApplicability.reason: A fleet-wide enforcement question answered by executing the runtime front door and loading the live policy snapshots for three hubs, plus a five-compiler trace and an N-to-1 manifest identity check.

targetSelection.selectionReason: Angle 13 names two questions — which preamble policy the runtime enforces, and whether identical leaf sets are defect or design; the enforcement answer lives in the compiler chain and the live engine, and the identity answer lives in the manifest, registry and generator contract.

searchLedger.invariant: Two artifacts describing the same hub policy must state it the same way.

searchActions.queryOrPath: routerPolicy.defaultResource vs ROUTER.md DEFAULT_RESOURCE blocks for all three hubs
searchActions.result: Two hubs state opposite existence; the third states different content and cardinality; the schema admits only a scalar.

searchLedger.rationale: The contradiction is fleet-wide, not hub-local, and the field shape is out of its own contract.

searchLedger.hypothesis: The compiled router loads the declared preamble before mode selection.

searchActions.queryOrPath: live loadSnapshot() policy for the three hubs, plus compiled-route.cjs executions
searchActions.result: No defaultResource key in any policy; no preamble field in any decision; DEFAULT_RESOURCE absent from the entire compiled-routing tree.

searchLedger.rationale: The enforcement answer is 'none'; the statements describe a behavior no code performs.

searchLedger.invariant: An N-to-1 alias fan-out keeps independently addressable leaf sets.

searchActions.queryOrPath: byte equality of the two improvement-lane arrays, alias-file presence, compiled-pipeline validation of manifest resources
searchActions.result: Arrays equal at 61; no alias file; pipeline enforces per-mode membership only, so identity passes.

searchLedger.rationale: The stated guarantee is unmet but no consumer depends on it, which bounds severity.

focus: Angle 14 — roster completeness for the seventh executor

findingDetails.title: cli-external-orchestration/ROUTER.md omits cli-hermes from all three prose roster statements while its own machine block and the compiled router carry the mode
findingDetails.evidence: cli-external-orchestration/ROUTER.md states a six-mode roster in all three prose statements (:24-25 hub-selects list, :46-64 per-mode leaf bullets with no cli-hermes bullet, :145-146 defer instruction to confirm the target executor) while the same file machine block names HERMES in INTENT_SIGNALS (:96) and RESOURCE_MAP (:124-126), mode-registry.json registers cli-hermes (:212-236), and compiled-route.cjs executed this iteration resolves hermes prompts to workflowMode cli-hermes.
findingDetails.impact: An agent following the hub's front-door doc sees six modes, has no leaf mapping for cli-hermes, and is told to confirm one of six executors; the machine block in the same file names seven, so the document disagrees with itself at the layer that governs manual routing. Wave-one F007 filed the same three statements at P0 and left one downgrade path (ROUTER.md shown superseded and marked non-authoritative); inspected this iteration, no supersession exists and SKILL.md:74 still names ROUTER.md the stage-two authority, so this lane adopts P0 on re-adjudication.
findingDetails.recommendation: Name cli-hermes in all three statements and add its leaf bullet, or replace the hand-written rosters with a pointer to mode-registry.json. No fix was made during this review.
findingDetails.scopeProof: Read ROUTER.md end to end (three roster sites confirmed, no seventh bullet), verified the HERMES intent and resource entries in the same file, confirmed the registry entry and executed the compiled route front door with hermes prompts. Re-read SKILL.md:74 and hub-router.json to test wave one's supersession downgrade path; both confirm ROUTER.md remains the designated stage-two authority.

findingDetails.title: Hub SKILL.md files carry hand-written mode counts their own registries contradict
findingDetails.evidence: cli-external-orchestration/SKILL.md:74 says the surface router defines the leaf-intent model for all six modes against :54 same file All seven modes are primary and 7 registered modes; system-deep-loop/SKILL.md:80 says the 3 improvement modes share the deep-improvement packet against 2 registered (agent-improvement, model-benchmark); system-deep-loop/SKILL.md:131 says six registered modes against 5 registered and description.json:3 five modes.
findingDetails.impact: Three count statements across two hub front doors misstate the mode set their own registries define; nothing reads prose counts, so the drift persists across releases.
findingDetails.recommendation: State counts from mode-registry.json, or drop the numeral and reference the registry. No fix was made during this review.
findingDetails.scopeProof: Parsed all three mode-registry.json files to count registered modes (5/6/7), read each numeric count statement at its line, and checked the sibling description.json statement in system-deep-loop for the correct count.

findingDetails.title: Deep-loop protocol and packet prose under-describes the executor set, and the council packet's prose contradicts its own resolver
findingDetails.evidence: deep-review/references/protocol/loop-protocol.md:281 closes the executor-resolution section with the seven-kind authority is executor-config.ts after naming cli-codex, cli-cursor, cli-devin, cli-pi and omitting cli-hermes (which executor-config.ts:11 declares and fanout-run.cjs:2721 implements; hermes appears nowhere in the review protocol); deep-research/SKILL.md:267 repeats the same seven-kind framing without hermes; deep-ai-council/SKILL.md:22 states the resolver accepts native/cli-opencode/cli-cursor/cli-devin/cli-pi/opencode while orchestrate-session.cjs:198 accepts cli-hermes and the same SKILL.md lists hermes rounds at :26 and :357; both council YAMLs repeat the short list at :26.
findingDetails.impact: A reader of any of these sentences under-provisions a supported capability; the council sentence reads the opposite of what the code does.
findingDetails.recommendation: Name cli-hermes in each enumeration (or reference EXECUTOR_KINDS), and correct the seven-kind count to the authority's eight. No fix was made during this review.
findingDetails.scopeProof: Read both loop protocols, the research SKILL section, the council SKILL sections and both council YAMLs at their lines, then traced the council accept list to the resolver code that permits cli-hermes.

findingDetails.title: Deep-loop catalogs describe the executor dispatcher as three kinds (twice with a duplicated kind name) against a driver that implements eight
findingDetails.evidence: deep-review/feature-catalog/feature-catalog.md:150 and loop-lifecycle/executor-selection-contract.md:3,:29-35 describe parseExecutorConfig as one of three dispatch branches (native, cli-opencode, cli-claude-code) against the 8-kind schema; runtime/feature-catalog/fanout/fanout-run.md:42 says Supports all 3 CLI kinds: cli-opencode, cli-claude-code, cli-opencode against fanout-run.cjs:2717-2722 eight adapters; deep-improvement model-dispatcher.md:27 says across cli-opencode, cli-claude-code, and cli-opencode against dispatch-model.cjs:138-145 six KNOWN_EXECUTORS; scripts/model-benchmark/README.md:75 says routes to cli-opencode or cli-claude-code.
findingDetails.impact: Four catalog sites understate what the dispatcher supports by 3-6 kinds, and the duplicated cli-opencode in two of them marks a botched rename that makes the wrong claim harder to notice.
findingDetails.recommendation: Correct the counts and kind names in the four sites from the source files; check for further duplicated-name substitutions in the same documents. No fix was made during this review.
findingDetails.scopeProof: Read each catalog claim at its line and compared it to the subject source: fanout-run.cjs adapter map (8) and dispatch-model.cjs KNOWN_EXECUTORS (6), both read directly.

findingDetails.title: cli-* packet sibling lists froze at each packet's authoring date, leaving the newest siblings out of six files
findingDetails.evidence: cli-claude-code/SKILL.md:381 lists cli-opencode twice and no cli-pi or cli-hermes; cli-codex/SKILL.md:383 names 2 siblings, cli-cursor/SKILL.md:416 three, cli-devin/SKILL.md:464 four, cli-pi/SKILL.md:303 five, while cli-hermes/SKILL.md:345 names all six; cli-devin/references/integration-patterns.md:30 still says Devin is the 5th executor kind in the cli-* family (5th of seven) and cli-pi/references/pi-tools.md:17 enumerates five sibling packets without cli-hermes; the four older packet READMEs do carry a cli-hermes row.
findingDetails.impact: Each older packet's prose roster omits at least the newest two siblings; the duplicate cli-opencode in cli-claude-code displaces cli-codex, so a reader cannot recover the intended list from the file.
findingDetails.recommendation: Update each sibling list (or replace it with a pointer to mode-registry.json), and fix the duplicated-name slots from the packet's intended provider. No fix was made during this review.
findingDetails.scopeProof: Read the Related-skills closure of all seven cli-* SKILL.md files plus both named reference files, and checked the packet README rows to confirm the READMEs were updated while the SKILL.md lists were not.

focus: Angle 15 — stale references in catalogs and READMEs
filesReviewed: 1,100 catalog, README and playbook documents path-scanned; ~90 read in context

findingDetails.title: All three hubs' compiled-routing catalog entries cite a superseded runtime-layout generation in nine places
findingDetails.evidence: Each hub's entry names .opencode/bin/lib/compiled-routing/011-runtime-engine/lib/resolve.cjs at :28 and :52 and .opencode/bin/lib/compiled-routing/010-live-activation/activation/<hub>/manifest.json at :28 and :53; the layout root holds 013-live-activation and 014-runtime-engine, and the live front-door dependency is 014-runtime-engine/lib/resolve.cjs (confirmed on disk). Wave-one F014 expansion from one hub to three.
findingDetails.impact: Every reader of any hub's compiled-routing inventory gets a resolution-order description written against paths no consumer uses; three hubs now disagree with the runtime they document.
findingDetails.recommendation: Repoint the nine citations to 013-live-activation and 014-runtime-engine in all three entries. No fix was made during this review.

targetSelection.selectionReason: Angle 15 names catalogs, READMEs and playbooks and the sweep must find cited paths, counts and claims the tree contradicts; the deprecation packet was added because the compiled path scan kept returning removed-lane artifacts.

reviewDepthApplicability.reason: A three-hub sweep over 1,100 documents with four counted catalog trees, two executed checkers and a removal-list census against the deprecation packet.

results.summary: The phase spec's five wave-two angles are each fully executed; every iteration ends partial because the reviewed artifacts cannot satisfy their own stated rosters, rules or references as written. No hard gate failure: the target is a review packet whose spec scopes the finding set rather than asserting a shipped contract.
The phase spec carries no per-iteration checklist rows; its REQ rows are assessed at synthesis.

Angle 15 completed the cited-path, count and layout-generation sweep: nine stale generation citations across three hubs, nine stale references in four classes, one count shortfall, one renamed extension and one stale command path. Catalog index integrity itself is sound in four of five catalogs.

Every playbook command and flag resolves, and the deep-review playbook's own scenario counts are correct, but its test cross-reference is a false absence claim, the council's names five renamed files, and the legacy README's validation block fails as written.
